## The base
### Separate base and payer schedules

For every component record cash compensation, taxable non-cash benefits, A-income, ordinary taxable income, exclusions, age/residence/coverage evidence, cumulative annual base, rate, payer and settlement route. The Health and employee AMEG bases are statutory taxable income; employer AMEG uses paid A-income. ALS and parental contributions use their own inclusion/exclusion lists. Do not add all published percentages and apply the sum to gross wages. [Health Act §24][health]; [AMEG Act §2][ameg]; [ALS Act §§7–8][als]; [Parental Act §§17–18][parental]

Health liability is tied to residence/coverage under §§1, 24, not merely A-income. Under Regulation 76/2024, qualifying Nordic social-insurance payment and the statutory no-deduction condition can support an application for exemption. Keep foreign coverage/payment, work-country/employer and Faroese-work-share evidence. Partial-year relief distinguishes monthly fixed charges and the income earned during the exempt period; a blanket annual exemption is not inferred. Notify cessation of foreign payment. [Health Act §24(2)][health]; [Regulation 76/2024 §§1–4][healthreg]

Employee AMEG ceases under the retirement-age rule, with Regulation 45/2024 §1(2) applying exemption from the start of the year the person reaches statutory pension age. A newcomer within three years of that age who has never previously had a Faroese home has a separate exception. Employer age does not exempt staff wages; employer liability remains on A-income under §2. Specified foreign FAS wages have their separate worker/employer exclusions. Nordic social-security coordination requires its actual application, not a generic EU assumption. [AMEG Act §2(2), (6)–(7)][ameg]; [Regulation §§1–3][amegreg]

ALS recipient liability starts at 16 and runs to statutory pension age. Payer liability has a different limb. Sections 7–8 address treaty-foreign social coverage, specified pension/adapted-work exemptions, benefit exclusions and foreign FAS categories. Temporary residence/work permits can support an application for up to one year at a time under §8(3), from receipt of the written application. Track the insured person's DKK 650,000 ceiling cumulatively across payers. Employer charges require their own base; do not transfer that personal limit to the employer. [ALS Act §§2, 7–9][als]

Parental recipient liability requires full Faroese tax liability, age at least 16 and below statutory pension age. The payer limb covers A-income paid in the Faroes, with §18's exclusions, including the specified pension/benefit and limited-tax-liability FAS income. Certain fully liable persons without a fixed Faroese home can apply for exemption from receipt of their application. Self-employed business income has a separate voluntary insurance route under §20, rather than automatically being the A-income charge. [Parental Act §§17–20][parental]

The occupational-disease contribution does not replace required work-injury insurance. Work Injury Act §79 distinguishes paid A-income for employers from prior-year taxable income for the self-employed. The wage-guarantee Act's foreign FAS exclusions and government-benefit payer exception must also be checked. [Work Injury Act §79][injury]; [Guarantee Act §7][guarantee]

Pension Act §1 covers a fully tax-liable person below statutory pension age, subject to civil-service-pension, qualifying student-foreign-income and other express exceptions. Section 3 excludes listed pensions, support/insurance amounts and qualifying foreign-pension/NAV situations. Section 17 separately addresses persons born before 1 January 1954 and the approved legacy Danish-provider transition. Do not replace those tests with a blanket “all adults pay 12%”. [Pension Act §§1–3, 17][pension]

Compute eligible combined A/B income, the statutory minimum, qualifying contributions already made and the DKK 150,000 annual mandatory ceiling. A contract can fund or require more. The employer must transfer pension with salary through TAKS's withholding system; incompatible transfers can be rejected. B-income has its own payment/part-year rules. Eligible paid contributions have ordinary income deduction/exclusion under §12(3)–(4), while pension contribution tax is withheld under §12(2). Keep gross pension, contribution tax, credited savings and any insurance allocation separate. [Pension Act §§2, 12][pension]

Use the operative pension rule for the event, not the latest consolidation alone. The contribution rate is **12% throughout 2026**. Keep the following dated ledger. [Pension Act §2(1)][pension]; [payment Regulation 60/2021 §1][pensionreg]

The older linked Regulation 14/1987 still describes the former fund/accounts and cannot override the later statute abolishing that fund. Current operational details need the checks in Sources. - **Proved employee payment:** reduce the relevant benefit value by the amount the employee proves was paid **to the employer for use of the employer's asset**, with a floor of **zero**. Record the asset, actual payment and proof. A payroll deduction or employee expense is not automatically that payment. Thus a full-year DKK 56,800 car benefit with DKK 5,000 proved qualifying payment gives **DKK 51,800**; payment of DKK 60,000 gives **zero**, not a negative benefit.

- **Proved lower private car use:** VLS D states that the standard car value corresponds to **10,000 private kilometres annually**. If actual private use is proved or substantiated below that figure, reduce proportionately, with a clear private/business mileage split. With a DKK 56,800 annual car value, use `56,800 × proved private km / 10,000` within this below-10,000-km route. A worker provided that car only from July through December, with a complete log proving **4,000 private km** over the year and no employee payment, has **DKK 22,720** under this route. Six months alone does not establish DKK 28,400: this example uses proved mileage, not a six-twelfths or 365-day convention. Missing logs do not establish zero private use. This source does not supply an above-standard-mileage uplift or the ordering of combined mileage and employee-payment adjustments.

## Cross-border points

Keep work-country, residence, treaty social-security coverage, FAS/bareboat status, payer, contract and exemption decisions together. Tax residence does not settle every social contribution. ALS's treaty-foreign coverage exception, Health's application regime, AMEG's FAS exceptions and mandatory pension's full-liability/foreign-plan conditions differ. Foreign-employer non-A wages can fall within ALS §2's domestic-work or Nordic-coverage routes. ### 1. Ordinary salary and employer-funded pension

Assume a fully liable 30-year-old resident with no exemption. A normal non-leave month's A-income and each statutory taxable-income base used here are independently established at DKK 30,000. The contract adds an employer-funded gross pension of DKK 3,600, outside that cash wage; assume the pension follows the 12% minimum and 40% provisional pension-tax route. ### 2. Annual limits belong to different schemes

Assume a fully eligible worker's annual ALS income is DKK 700,000 and no other payer has used the limit. Employee ALS is 0.6% of DKK 650,000, or DKK 3,900. The employer's independently established liable wage base is DKK 700,000, giving DKK 4,200; the personal cap is not duplicated for the employer. Separately, assume an individual's eligible annual pension base is DKK 1,500,000 and no contribution has yet been credited. Twelve percent is DKK 180,000, but the mandatory gross ceiling is DKK 150,000. If paid at a verified 40% final pension-tax rate, tax is DKK 60,000 and credited pension DKK 90,000 before insurance allocation. The DKK 30,000 excess is outside the statutory minimum, not an automatically permitted unpaid contractual contribution. These are two independent limit checks; no total net pay is claimed. ## Who this applies to

Under Tax Act §37a, covered relationships include foreign control, control of legal persons, common-group entities and foreign/Faroese permanent establishments. Control generally requires **more than 50%** of capital or votes; indirect holdings, related persons and joint-control agreements matter. Denmark and Greenland count as foreign jurisdictions. Section 118a separately requires controlled-transaction disclosure, including domestic relationships. Test both provisions rather than assuming identical wording. [Current Tax Act, §§37a and 118a][law]

This Guide addresses pricing and documentation. It includes the statutory thin-capitalisation screen below. PE existence, corporate residence, country-by-country reporting and treaty relief require their separate analyses.

## The base

Use independent-party prices and terms for covered transactions. Keep the ownership chart and voting agreements distinct: multiplication of economic ownership does not establish voting control. [Tax Act §37a][law]

TAKS's older guidance recommends a transaction inventory covering goods, services, financing, intangibles and other economic dealings. Document functions, assets, risks, contracts and comparables; explain the selected method for each transaction type. Its methods include CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM and profit split. A single method is not automatically suitable throughout a group. Its DKK 500,000 discussion is **not a blanket exemption for smaller dealings**. [TAKS guidance, pages 8–13][guidance]

Practical workpaper: reconcile each counterparty total to the ledger, identify the pricing evidence available when the transaction occurred, and record why any proposed adjustment follows from that evidence. An illustrative markup is never a safe harbour. The documentation must support an assessment of arm's-length terms, not merely list invoices. [Tax Act §118a(4)][law]
### Separate thin-capitalisation calculation

Tax Act §37b applies where a §1 company has debt to a §118a(1) related party and its year-end debt/equity ratio exceeds 4:1. Deny interest and exchange-loss deductions on the controlled-debt portion exceeding that boundary, unless the company proves comparable financing could be obtained between independent parties. A pricing study supporting the interest rate alone does not establish that financing-volume exception. Third-party debt guaranteed directly or indirectly by the specified owners or group is treated as controlled debt. Exactly 4:1 does not exceed the ratio test. [§37b(1)][law]

Use year-end **market value** of the statutory financial-claim and convertible debt. Equity is market value of assets less that debt; related-party equity contributions count only to the extent they remain for at least two years. Do not substitute accounting net assets without this reconciliation. For a simple positive-equity case where all relevant debt is controlled, identify excess debt as max(0, debt − 4 × equity), then trace the interest and exchange losses actually attributable to that excess. Mixed borrowing, different rates, zero/negative equity and valuation disputes need a supported allocation beyond that simple formula. Disallowed exchange losses can offset later exchange gains on the same loan under §37b(1); do not infer a corresponding general carryforward for disallowed interest. [§37b(1)–(3)][law]

Apply §37b(4)'s combined asset/debt calculation where companies fall under the statutory common control: eliminate participating-company shares and intercompany claims/debts as directed. The rule also applies to foreign-company Faroese PEs, using only connected PE assets/debts under subsection 6. The detailed ownership/family and voting provisions in subsection 5 control the group perimeter. Retain the market-value and two-year capital evidence with the financing comparables. [§37b(4)–(6)][law]
## Deadlines and filing
Disclose transaction type and volume on the tax return. Required written documentation must reach TAKS within **60 days of its request**. [§118a(1), (4)][law]

TAKS's company-return guidance gives **1 July** as the ordinary return deadline. Accounts accompany the return and must be submitted through Borgaragluggin. A justified extension requires application; the published outer limit is **15 August**. Preserve the actual extension decision. [TAKS tax returns][returns]
Do not substitute the Danish documentation timetable. Retrieve the current Faroese return and appendices for the relevant filing year; the 2017 PDF's form identifier is historical.
## Penalties and interest

Missing required documentation permits estimated assessment under §118a(5). That subsection also requires approval from Stýrið before the tax authority makes an arm’s-length income adjustment. Tax Act §141(1)(3) provides a fine for intentional or grossly negligent failure to supply information required by §§118–124; the provision states no fixed amount. Evasion intent or other aggravating circumstances can raise punishment to detention or imprisonment up to two years under §141(2). False/misleading information used for tax assessment/control has separate §§139–140 exposure. Do not describe estimated assessment as the only consequence. [Tax Act §§139–141][law]

Ordinary company late-payment interest is 0.7% per commenced month under §81(2), subject to §146's separate under-assessment rule, including its specified 12% annual company interest. These are not flat TP-documentation fines. The actual assessment and offence facts determine the applicable route. [Tax Act §§81, 146][law] [§118a(5)][law]
## Cross-border points

Evaluate the relevant treaty and any corresponding-adjustment procedure separately. The older English guidance is useful for analytical examples but predates the 2019 documentation exemption. It cannot establish current filing obligations on its own. The separate [CbCR Guide](fo-country-by-country-reporting.md) applies its own group-revenue, notification and exchange tests; a documentation exemption here does not establish a CbCR exemption.

Tax Act §37a(4) permits avoidance of specified secondary consequences by undertaking payment on the corrected terms, subject to its foreign-authority taxation condition in the stated cross-border cases. Preserve actual acceptance/payment and foreign treatment; do not treat a journal entry alone as treaty corresponding relief. Ordinary amendment limits for §§37a, 37b and 118a matters are five years under Tax Administration Act §8, with different start points for authority action and taxpayer requests. Treaty mutual-agreement deadlines and exceptional reopening need their own review. [Tax Act §37a(4)][law]; [Tax Administration Act §§8–9][admin]

## Who this applies to

VAT but input recovery, and exempt activities without input recovery. The
Faroese VAT territory and charge arise under Act 136/1992 §§1–3. Foreign
business activity can require registration independently of income-tax PE
status. Danish/EU VAT rules are not a substitute for this Act ([law][law]).
Section 4 exempts annual sales **below DKK 50,000**. Exactly DKK 50,000 does
not satisfy that wording. Determine annual business sales rather than profit,
and separate the exempt activities under §2(3). A registered business does
not stop accounting for VAT solely because later sales fall below the
threshold; TAKS describes cancellation as a separate choice where turnover
stays low ([§§4–5][law]; [TAKS tourism guidance][tourism]).
Register at least eight days before activity starts, subject to the security
provisions. Businesses with the same owner are generally notified together,
with separate-registration requests possible for separate accounts. Approved
joint registration is treated as one business; joint liabilities apply.

person/local establishment unless the Hoyvík treaty exception applies.

## The base
### Sales classification and taxable amount
Standard-rated value is the consideration excluding MVG. Include relevant
other duties, packaging, freight/insurance, connection/establishment charges,
commissions and financing supplements. Separately evidenced interest on the
outstanding purchase price can be outside the value under §7(3). Owner/
non-business withdrawals generally use purchase/production cost; barter uses
the ordinary selling price or the specified calculated price. Connected-party
value can be adjusted under §9 ([§§7–9 and 11][law]).
Exempt §2(3) services include qualifying healthcare, social care, education,
certain cultural activity, sport, passenger transport with the bus exception,
specified postal services, property letting/management, insurance/finance,
gaming, artistic activity, funeral services, tourist-guide/agency services,
water supply and the tightly conditioned charity second-hand shop. The
exceptions inside each category matter: a concert or commercial non-route
bus service is not automatically exempt because it is cultural/transport.
Restaurant and bar sales are not hotel-room sales ([§2(3)][law]).
Section 12 separately excludes listed supplies from output-taxable sales,
including exports and qualifying services abroad, directly linked foreign
freight, specified foreign-account goods work/design, qualifying ships/
aircraft and work on them, newspapers, listed books/audiobooks, specified
fishing supplies, hotel/guesthouse rooms and camping sites, prescription
medicine, specified vegetables and baby nappies. Use the actual item/code
and conditions. TAKS confirms the zero-output/input-recovery distinction for
qualifying accommodation. A §2 exempt activity has a different input result
([§12][law]; [TAKS tourism guidance][tourism]).
The tax period follows actual supplies. Timely invoices can determine the
supply timing under §13(2). For an advance received before supply/invoicing,
80% of the gross advance enters the taxable-sales base; standard VAT on that
base is 20% of the gross receipt. Returns, established bad debts and later
collections adjust their statutory 80% bases. Discounts requiring later
conditions need the prescribed credit-note treatment. Do not treat an unpaid
invoice as an established bad debt automatically ([§13][law]).
### Input recovery and mixed activity
Deduct supported supplier VAT invoiced in the period and the import VAT
imposed under §27, only with the eligible-use rules and invoice/customs
proof. Direct fully recoverable activity gets its supported input; direct
exempt/nonregistered activity gets none. Shared expenditure uses recoverable
activity sales excluding VAT divided by total sales for the accounting year.
Prior-year sales support provisional periods, with a final adjustment after
year end; a new business uses its actual period sales. Private use requires
a supported business-use estimate, not an invented flat percentage
Section 16(3) blocks specified food for proprietor/staff, owner/staff housing,
benefits in kind, staff welfare/holiday facilities and gifts. Apply the
express statutory exceptions rather than importing another country's
entertainment percentage. Property construction allocation uses relevant
business-building costs; equal-standard rooms can use floor area. Direct
repair costs follow the relevant rooms; common repairs use the prescribed
area proportion. Housing and non-optioned letting are excluded from business
rooms for this purpose ([§16(3)][law]; [regulation §§3–4][reg]).
For vehicles at most **3,500 kg actual total weight**, purchase/lease input
needs exclusive use in taxable sales activity; mixed private use does not
create a proportional purchase deduction. Vehicles over that weight follow
the specified business-use rules. Operating costs have a separate full-input
rule even with partial business use; **lease payments are not operating
costs** for it. Regulation §5 also requires annual taxable sales exceeding
**DKK 20,000**. Retain weight, use, sales and cost classification evidence
([regulation §5][reg]).
### Capital adjustments, sale and cessation
Maintain an asset register with original VAT, acquisition year, initial
recovery proportion, current use and remaining adjustment years. Annual
adjustment compares current recovery with acquisition-year recovery:
`original VAT × proportion change × 1/5` for equipment, or `× 1/10` for
property/qualifying works. A change **below ten percentage points** is
outside the annual adjustment requirement; exactly ten is not below it.
The regulation restricts upward adjustments where there was no original
recovery or a prior full nonrecoverable-use adjustment. Full nonrecoverable
use and specified transfers can accelerate the remaining period. A buyer's
assumption needs the actual eligibility and written acknowledgement, not
an automatic carryover ([regulation §§10–16][reg]).
Sales of business machinery/stock and withdrawals at deregistration are
within §11(4), subject to the specific exceptions. A transfer of a whole
business or part to a new operator running a registered business can fall
outside output-taxable sales under §12(5). Notify TAKS of the new operator,
address and transferred asset sale price within eight days. Property and
capital-adjustment succession still require their own conditions. Disposal
of a vehicle whose acquisition VAT could not be deducted has the separate
rule in regulation §9(3) ([§§11–12][law]; [regulation §§9, 12–14][reg]).

specified events, work/valuations on local movables, telecoms and broadcasts.

business entitled to recover all the VAT. Its list omits item 7; do not

Those items include rights, advertising, professional/advisory/data services,
staff supply, restraint obligations and intermediaries. They keep service
records for five years and pay/notify within ten days of service receipt.
Paragraph 4 does not state the supplier's DKK 50,000 threshold.
- Imported services equivalent to an exempt domestic supply have paragraph
6's exemption. Test that exemption before computing a charge.

full-recovery exclusion does not apply. A foreign supplier within paragraph
